title: Strict hot spots on simply connected planar domains
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that on a bounded simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary no eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has an interior critical point; consequently its maximum and minimum are attained only on the boundary. This is the simply connected hot-spots conjecture of Burdzy, in strict form and for every eigenfunction, the eigenvalue being allowed to be multiple. The first lesson fixes the setting and the named analytic facts (SOB) and (ER), constructs the eigenvalue problems, proves Filonov's strict inequality between the first positive Neumann eigenvalue and the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, and states the theorem. The second proves Hopf's lemma, builds a conformal map from the disc that is smooth up to the boundary, transfers the mean-zero condition to a positive boundary weight, proves that two paths with alternating endpoints in the disc meet, and deduces connected sign sets and the multiplicity bound. The third proves Rohleder's variational principle for tangent vector fields, with its equality case, and the curvature identity. The fourth builds the Green function and Poisson kernel of the disc with a subcritical potential, the kernels K, R, N and the boundary energy, and proves the multiplier identity. The fifth proves that the kernel K(p,s)K(p,t)/N(s,t) is conditionally negative semidefinite, through matrices with one positive eigenvalue, a regularized Green kernel, rank-one updates, quadrature and boundary limits. The sixth embeds the circle in a Hilbert space with this squared distance and proves the theorem.
prerequisites: course Elliptic operators and boundary problems, lesson Boundary energy, local inverses, and harmonic data: the energy solution of the Dirichlet problem (B10), the Poincare inequality (B11), the zero-trace space (B6), and H^2 and smooth regularity of the Dirichlet problem (B29)

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (SOB): Gauss-Green for bounded planar open sets with C^1 boundary; density of C^infinity up to the boundary in H^k, the trace H^1 -> L^2 of the boundary with kernel H^1_0 and dense range, Rellich compactness, and the Sobolev embedding H^(k+2) into C^k up to the boundary, on bounded planar domains with smooth boundary (Showalter, EJDE Monograph 01, Chapter II, Theorems 3.3, 4.2, 5.5, 5.8). The zero-trace description for C^1 boundaries is in the programme ((B6) of Boundary energy, local inverses, and harmonic data); the other statements are not proved in the programme.

Named hypothesis (ER): regularity of all orders for the Dirichlet and Neumann problems of the Laplacian on bounded planar domains with smooth boundary (Showalter, Chapter III, Theorems 6.1, 6.4, 6.5). The programme proves the Dirichlet case for L^2 data and for smooth data ((B29) of Boundary energy, local inverses, and harmonic data); the Neumann problem and the intermediate Dirichlet orders are not proved in the programme.
Missing foundation: a lesson on Sobolev spaces of smooth bounded domains (traces, Rellich compactness, embeddings) and on regularity for the Neumann problem would close (SOB) and (ER).

Not in the course: the reduction of Burdzy (arXiv:2610.12622, 8 Oct 2026; independently Banuelos) of a non-strict hot-spots statement on bounded simply connected planar domains with compact Neumann resolvent and simple eigenvalue to the smooth theorem. Its proof has not been checked here; candidate for a later lesson.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
